In spite of the story, the game works and has some decent puzzles, so I'm going to recommend it.

But BOY HOWDY is Artifex Mundi bad at mythology. This was the equivalent of telling me that Loki and Whisky Jack are the same person. I suppose you CAN mix Greco-Roman and northern European myth, but why on earth would you? 

The protagonist is also dumb as a rock, but that's to be expected.

A pretty standard hidden object game. Nothing particularly special about it, but enjoyable overall. Typical gameplay, pleasant visuals & soundtrack, and a fairly short experience (I finished easy mode in a couple hours). The voice acting was a little off, but that kinda seems par for the course for this genre tbh. I did get caught off guard by the implication that the game starts in Paris, when every voice in the game is either American or British-

As for the story, it's...alright. I'm really just being nitpicky about it. It's about Greek mythos, but I noticed some Scandinavian/Germanic stuff mixed in; it's mainly visual, with the very prominent exception of the dwarf character. Also, I was very confused about how the Minotaur got a whole-ass castle LMAO

Overall, a very standard experience across the board, but a fair choice if you're looking to scratch the HO game itch. Get it on sale.

[h1]Mythic vibes, light on actual HOG[/h1]

Playtime: 3h24m • Completion: 72% achievements (remaining ones are filler/perfect-score chasers)

[b]TL;DR:[/b] Strong mythology-driven story with good atmosphere and that polished Artifex Mundi look. But for a game sold as a HOG, there are only ~10 hidden-object scenes, and several puzzles lean on creaky, out-of-fashion motifs (think 7th Guest/11th Hour leftovers). Full price (€15) = no-go for ~3 hours; okay in a deep sale/bundle. Conditional Recommend (sale only).

[h2]What clicks[/h2]

Story & myth: Surprisingly well executed; the Minotaur thread carries the campaign.

Atmosphere & music: Sets a consistent mood; audio does some heavy lifting.

Art style: Clean, vibrant AM-house style—scenes are nice to look at.

[h2]What drags[/h2]

Too few HOGs: Only about ten; the HOG-to-puzzle ratio feels off for the label.

Outdated puzzle beats: A handful of “that old chestnut” designs that were already tired in classic FMV puzzlers.

Achievements: Remaining ones are filler/perfect-score—padding rather than meaningful goals.

[b]Value take[/b]

Full price (€15): 3/10 — not enough content/challenge to justify it.

Deep sale/bundle (≈-80%): acceptable for a mythic evening.

[b]Short & Dirty Ratings[/b] (10 = best)

Story/Mythology: 8.5

Atmosphere/Music: 8

Art/Environments: 8

Hidden-Object Content: 4 (too sparse)

Puzzle Design: 5 (some stale patterns)

Length/Replay: 5

Value: 3 (full price) / 7 (deep sale)

Overall: 6/10 — Conditionally Recommended (on sale/bundle).

Verdict: If you want a myth-heavy casual adventure with pretty scenes and a solid vibe, this delivers. If you came for lots of HOG scenes or fresher puzzle design, adjust expectations—or wait for a discount.

I liked this game a lot, it has that classic adventure feel to it that these fantasy type of games do. I just finished a spate of playing games that were more like the real world with supernatural elements to them, so this was as welcome return to form. I think that I just like the freedom they have with storylines and and ideas more in the fantasy setting games.

The story is a twist on an old story of mythology, and I liked it just fine. Not the best of these games, but definitely acceptable and was fun to follow. The music was pretty good, I found myself noticing how much I liked it when I was playing and the puzzles were good too. There was a nice variety of both normal puzzles and hidden object scenes. The hidden object scenes even had the variations where sometimes you are following a list of items in text, sometimes you're looking for a collection of objects to assemble something, or sometimes you are finding and using items in the scene in a certain order to eventually find one single item. Just really good classic gameplay.

I will also say the colors, the animations, the quality of the scenes were all very good, very vibrant with a lot of colors that I missed while playing gothic or pirate-themed games.

If I have any criticisms, it's mostly three things. First, some of the puzzles were a little too easy sometimes. Some were hard, so it's balanced, but you might find some to not be very challenging. The second was that the collectibles are genuinely hard to find. I had to play through twice to get them all because they way they are designed, some specifically call your attention but then others are placed in an area with the same pattern and color and they're almost invisible. And then the last thing was that the pacing could be weird at times. I usually feel like the way items you can pick up are paced on most games you never have so much in your inventory that you need to scroll through it horizontally. This game you always seemed to have a ton of things in your inventory.

But even though these are criticisms, I could see how some people would like them too. I didn't really have a huge problem. A nice, easy puzzle is fun to ace sometimes. Having a lot of items to use all at once can make you think a bit more about where to use them and be an extra challenge. The collectible issue for me was really the biggest thing and I wish this game had a collectible indicator in the HUD that tells you if you have a collectible in that scene to pick up, but it does not. Even then, some people might really enjoy seeking difficult collectibles out. So even the criticisms are kind of just preferences.

"Endless Fables" refers to something other than the game itself.  The weakness of The Minotaur's Curse is its length - it ends so soon!.  I finished the main story and the bonus adventure in just over three hours.  So, you may want to pick up the whole Endless Fables series in a bundle to make sure you've got enough Fables to keep you entertained.  I only have this game, so I'll get the rest later.

После длительного перерыва игры жанра hidden object стали вновь меня притягивать. Перспектива многочасового решения загадок и неспешного протыкивания поверхностей была для меня особенно заманчивой и желанной. Именно поэтому я вновь забрался в свой бездонный ящик с играми и присмотрел для себя несколько проектов с подобной тематикой.

Думаю многие в детстве увлекались "Легендами и Мифами Древней Греции". Моим проводником в мир увлекательных приключений в свое время стал Н.А. Кун, который посвящал меня в мрачные тайны античной эпохи. Путешествия Аргонавтов, подвиги Геракла и секс-приключения Зевса - в то время меня мало интересовало медиапространство и окружающий мир в целом, ведь я с головой погрузился в удивительный фантастический мир. Легенда о Минотавре и его история рождения восхищала меня, но одновременно с этим вызывала отвращение. Какого же было мое удивление, когда я узнал что в первой части саги Endless Fables мы сможем бросить вызов этому легендарному мифическому чудовищу и положить конец его кровавой жатве. Наша героиня по имени Памела Кавендиш известный археолог и ученый, поэтому когда она обнаруживает загадочный артефакт по названием "нить Ариадны", она уже знает с кем ей предстоит сразиться. Путеводная нить ведет нашу героиню прямиком в хитроумную ловушку и девушке предстоит проявить всю свою смекалку, чтобы не стать жертвой мифического чудовища.

Перед нами классический hidden object с уже знакомым нам набором загадачек. Переставление дисков, поиск спрятанных объектов, запоминание символов и правильная расстановка объектов - ветераны этого игрового жанра не увидят здесь для себя ничего нового. Другое дело сеттинг и сюжет. С самого начала игра погружает нас с головой в бурлящий экшен, где наша героиня будет попадать в самые разнообразные неприятности. Медуза Горгона, лесные нимфы и подземелья с горами трупов - воистину на земле есть места, куда не следует совать свой нос. На протяжении всего игрового процесса нас будут сопровождать различные живописные пейзажи и множество точек интереса. Даже сюжет здесь смог меня порадовать и заинтересовать до такой степени, что заставило меня пробежать игру буквально на одном дыхании. Любителей hidden object искренне приглашаю отправиться в это античное путешествие за порцией новых впечатлений. 6 часов чистейшего удовольствия и релакса вам точно обеспечены.

Classic Artifex Mundi HOG. This one is particularly magical based on Greek Mythology. it's got a Minotaur and Medusa but it's not overly Greek aesthetic-wise, I mean there's also a leprechaun and a steampunk owl in it. 

Story-wise I had no clue what really was going on, it didn't make sense to me but I also don't play hogs for the stories personally so I didn't pay much attention to it during my playthrough. It can be really hit or miss with HOGs whether you're going to get an engaging story or not and it doesn't bother me personally but I know some people play these games for the stories too so if that's what you're looking for I'm not sure you're gonna get it with this one. 

One thing that bothered me a little which is probably my own idiosyncrasy is that they didn't really justify the minotaur character nor were they really consistent with using the minotaurs mythological tropes. You look at the figure of the minotaur in mythology and such and it can have an allegorical meaning i.e. ancient greek mystery cults, it has analogs in the constellations like taurus and aquarius, the minotaur can be a useful character to tell a good story or share a moral lesson or something (you know, like a fable) but you don't see any reference to that stuff here. 

I don't know why they chose a minotaur for this game, seemed a bit arbitrary, might as well have been a shadowy robed figure. It's kind of all over the place and didn't really seem consistent or coherent to me. It's more like they just chose random characters and wrote a virtually non existent story and the only value the game has is if you already enjoy playing hidden object games and looking at the artwork which is probably the main reason why most people play these games to be honest.

 "Endless Fables: The Minotaur's Curse" is just 1 in a million other HOGs you could play. I don't see any particular reason to pick this one other than if you like the artwork (which is very nice btw) and maybe want or have the other games in the "endless fables" series.

Endless Fables: The Minotaur's Curse provided a surprisingly good detective story that while still being challenging with it's variety of puzzles, didn't overdo them. If I had to describe the difficulty in better terms, it would be that the game is geared towards young adults or teens based on content and difficulty. The overall gameplay is intuitive and easy to grasp with an intuitive tutorial that players can choose to use at the beginning of the game, and dependent on the difficulty chosen. The storyline that the game also went with was interesting and followed the original pretty well. It also did expand a bit beyond with the presence of Ariadne's thread but not by much. I'd love to have seen this function used more than in just a few places.

While the game is short I found that there could be a few QOL changes that would benefit the game. For achievement hunters like myself, the inability to choose to play back specific levels after beating the game becomes a bit tedious, especially if you are also hunting for all the additional goodies along the way. I also appreciated the voice-acting here and there but it felt few and far between. When it was present it sounded awkward and didn't always fit the mood the game was trying to provide, in this sense I almost think the game would have been better off without any voice acting, or at least an option to turn off just the mc's voice as the other characters weren't too bad. A final point comes to the playtime versus the price point. I am a firm believer in getting my money's worth from a game with a 1:1 system. For every hour I play I expect to spend at least a dollar. In this sense the game is priced a bit high for the short playtime I had that included two full playthroughs, and the start of a third. 

The overall art of the game was pretty to look at but with foliage areas did appear a bit busy and difficult to navigate at times. There is also a small section where there is a hidden goodie next to the hitbox for the entrance to a barn that makes the object difficult to grab due to the overlap. Thankfully, this was the only location I ended up having that trouble. The lighting of the levels was bright enough to easily be able to pick out aspects of the level while also keeping a constant mood in both the lighter events and darker toned events. 

Achievements in the game aren't too difficult to get and are not difficulty locked. If you play on casual you are able to get every achievement, if you struggle with some of the minigame or HOL achievements there is an option to just play these from the starting menu so you don't have to go through the game multiple times for a single puzzle. 

Based on all of the above while Endless Fables: The Minotaur's Curse isn't a bad game, it's definitely not the greatest of it's genre on the market. However, if you are just starting to get into games of this genre, or are intrigued then this would be a great starting point instead of trying some of the more well known titles that tend to play towards a more adult audience than this game does while also featuring some beautiful artwork.

Speaking of. There are many achievements in the game, and a few of them requires you to have keen eye for details. Anyway! Ofc I recommend this game. I really enjoyed playing a game like this again.
